title: ～させる — causative (“make / let someone ～”)
summary: The causative form, for making or letting someone do something. Group 1: ない-stem + せる; group 2: stem + させる; する → させる; 来る → 来させる.

patterns.gloss: Group 1: ない-stem + せる (読む → 読ませる)
Group 2: stem + させる (食べる → 食べさせる)

body.p: With intransitive verbs (寝る, 行く) mark the person made to act with を (子どもを寝させる). With transitive verbs (読む, 掃除する) use に (弟に掃除させる).
It can mean forcing or allowing. It is basically for someone with authority telling someone below them to act, so it is rude to use for a superior.

examples.ja: 母（はは）は弟（おとうと）に部屋（へや）を掃除（そうじ）させました。
examples.romaji: Haha wa otōto ni heya o sōji sasemashita.
examples.tr: My mother made my brother clean his room.

examples.ja: 先生（せんせい）は学生（がくせい）に本（ほん）を読（よ）ませた。
examples.romaji: Sensei wa gakusei ni hon o yomaseta.
examples.tr: The teacher made the students read a book.

examples.ja: 母（はは）は子（こ）どもを早（はや）く寝（ね）させた。
examples.romaji: Haha wa kodomo o hayaku nesaseta.
examples.tr: The mother made the child go to sleep early.

pitfalls: Intransitive verbs take を, transitive verbs take に for the person.
Do not use ～させる toward a superior.
